stories.title: Mayor of Mold to raise funds for good causes at food festival
stories.summary: Mold Town Council will have a presence at this year’s Mold Food and Drink Festival, running from 18 to 20 September. Representatives will be at the Totally Mold marquee throughout Saturday and Sunday to meet residents and visitors. The Mayor of Mold, Councillor Jo Edwards, will also attend the festival across the weekend. Cllr Edwards

stories.title: Free childcare for eligible two-year-olds in Flintshire from November
stories.summary: Flintshire County Council has opened applications for funded childcare places for two-year-olds living in eligible areas of the county. Applications opened on 1 September, with places available from 2 November. The scheme is run through the Welsh Government’s Flying Start programme. stories.title: Martyn’s Law: Northop college adds anti-terrorism qualifications to business courses
stories.summary: Businesses and organisations across North Wales can prepare for landmark new anti-terrorism legislation with specialist qualifications at Coleg Cambria. The college’s Northop Business School is offering NEBOSH National Certificates designed to support those affected by the Terrorism (Protection of Premises) Act 2025 – widely known as Martyn’s Law. stories.title: Flintshire resident seeking 100% council tax rebate after bins not collected for six months
stories.summary: A resident on a Flintshire new-build housing estate which has not had a single bin collection for six months has requested a 100% council tax rebate as compensation.
